tier_reason: The README gives first-party ratios against PNG (about 20x faster compression, about 2x faster decompression of 24-bit PPM) with no benchmark program, test images, PNG implementation, compiler or CPU; main.cpp is only a PPM-to-IZ converter with no timing code. Ratios without methodology are tier C.

corrections.baseline: PNG (format only; the README never names the PNG implementation, tool or compression level, so libpng/zlib is inferred)
corrections.stars_or_usage: 53 stars, 22 forks; repackaged for ROS as the imagezero package and swri-robotics/imagezero_transport (37 stars)
corrections.caveats: Only a README paragraph backs the claim: no benchmark code, test images, CPU, compiler or PNG implementation, so the baseline is inferred (low confidence). The repository was archived on 2022-09-14 and its last commit is 2013-11-06, so the comparison predates modern libpng, zlib-ng and libdeflate. The author calls the code 'early work in progress' with no fixed format or API, and the WARNING file says it must be built with full optimization or the non-inlined predictors cause an access violation (CMake sets -O2 -mmmx -mtune=atom). It handles only 24-bit RGB, no alpha or grayscale, which is why nigeltao/qoir left it out of its benchmark. The only independent number found is an informal 2018 gist (awesomebytes, i7-6700HQ, ROS Kinetic, 640x320 at 30 fps) where the subscribing node used 82-84% CPU with imagezero versus 108% with PNG at levels 3 and 9, a CPU-usage observation rather than a throughput benchmark.

notes: Claim text matches the README exactly; no repository file measures anything. The ROS announcement (discourse.openrobotics.org) and the 2012 LWN article were EGRESS_BLOCKED, so any numbers there were not checked; the swri-robotics/imagezero_transport README only repeats the 20x/2x sentence.

tier_reason: The README names libpng explicitly and states a single first-party ratio ('twice as fast as libpng' on x86/x86-64/ARM) with no data or method. The repository's lodepng_benchmark.cpp is the stock lodepng benchmark: it includes only lodepng.h and times lodepng encode/decode, so nothing in the repo measures libpng. A stated ratio without methodology is tier C.

corrections.workload: PNG decoding only (lodepng decoder with SIMD unfiltering from the simdtests/depng submodule and libdeflate inflate); the README describes no images, sizes or methodology.
corrections.caveats: The libpng baseline is named in the README, but the only evidence is the sentence 'twice as fast as libpng'; the repository's lodepng_benchmark.cpp times lodepng alone and never links libpng, and no CPU, compiler, images or libpng/zlib versions are given. The Makefile builds the library with -O2 -fomit-frame-pointer. Output-correctness fixes landed on 2019-01-21 ('average/paeth of first line') and 2019-01-22 ('If scanline is not a multiple of 4 bytes, the operation was not correct'), at the same time as the README edits, so the speed claim may predate those fixes. The last commit is 2019-01-22, so the comparison predates current libpng (which has its own SIMD filters) and current libdeflate. This is a code derivative of lodepng (its LICENSE carries Lode Vandevenne's copyright) rather than a GitHub fork. The predecessor kanryu/simd_lode_png states a 5x goal with no measurements.

notes: Baseline libpng is stated, not inferred, but no measurement against it exists anywhere in the repository; the 2x figure is an unsupported README claim, kept at C under the numbers-without-methodology rule (it could equally be read as D). No third-party measurement was found.

tier_reason: All README table numbers match the record and come from public first-party programs examples/image/png_benchmark/png_benchmark.cpp and examples/image/jpeg_benchmark/jpeg_benchmark.cpp with the CPU named, but the compiler and the exact flags used for the README runs are not stated, so it falls short of A and stays C.

corrections.baseline: libpng (via find_module(PNG), version and zlib build not stated); 'libjpeg' is whatever jpeglib.h find_module(JPEG) linked, used through the libjpeg API one scanline at a time. Every current install path in docs/installation/setup.md and vcpkg.json installs libjpeg-turbo, but the library used for the i9-8950HK table run is not recorded.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the README runs. Repository defaults: CMake Release build, ENABLE_SSE4 on and AVX/AVX2 off for the mango library, and png_benchmark adds -mavx2 -mpclmul on x86.
corrections.workload: One timed run per library on one image each: PNG decode from memory and RGBA8 encode to a file (2560x1600 and 4833x5875 PNGs on an i7-11800H); JPEG decode from file and encode to file (5184x3456 and 2560x1600 JPEGs on an i9-8950HK). Milliseconds per image plus output size.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README tables: PNG decode 3.2 ms vs libpng 57.3 ms (2560x1600) and 53.7 ms vs 379.5 ms (4833x5875); PNG encode 57.2 ms vs 820.5 ms and 287.0 ms vs 14051.3 ms; JPEG decode 23.3 ms vs libjpeg 197.8 ms (5184x3456) and 3.2 ms vs 32.9 ms (2560x1600); JPEG encode 18.5 ms vs 70.1 ms and 4.3 ms vs 16.3 ms. That is about 18x PNG decode and 8.5x JPEG decode on the first image of each pair (derived from page data). Mango ran its default multi-threaded path; the baselines ran single-threaded.
corrections.caveats: Both benchmark programs run mango multi-threaded by default (g_option_multithread / args.multithread = true, --nomt to disable) against single-threaded libpng and libjpeg, and no single-threaded mango numbers are published. The PNG decode figures most likely apply to mango-written files: mango's encoder by default (ImageEncodeOptions::parallel = true) writes a custom pLLD chunk with independently compressed segments, its decoder then takes the parallel decode_plld path, and both test images have an input size equal to mango's own encoded size (3531 KB and 33598 KB). Ordinary PNGs go through the single-stream decode_std path, so the 18x decode lead does not carry over to arbitrary PNGs. In PNG encode mango uses zlib level 4 with parallel segments against libpng defaults, and its output is about 24% larger on the first image (3531 vs 2843 KB) and 19% larger on the second (33598 vs 28180 KB) (derived from page data). In JPEG encode libjpeg runs at quality 95 and mango at quality 0.70. Each library is timed once, including file I/O. png_benchmark prints the fractional digit as microseconds mod 10 rather than tenths of a millisecond (cosmetic, under 0.1 ms). Commit 2a974fb (2026-09-29) fixed a wrong-operand bug in the SSE/AVX2/AVX-512 JPEG iDCT that produced incorrect output, and 17c019c fixed the NEON iDCT; whether that bug was present when the JPEG tables were measured is not established (jpeg_idct.cpp was refactored on 2026-08-15). The two table pairs use different CPUs, and the README itself quotes randy408 (the libspng author's handle): 'I'm skeptical of those benchmarks.' The license is the standard zlib text under a 'MANGO' header; bundled third-party code was not audited.

notes: Numbers are real and code-backed, but the headline gaps come mostly from multi-threading plus mango's own parallel-segment PNG layout (the test PNGs appear to be mango-encoded), and JPEG encode compares different quality settings; the enricher should say so. The JPEG baseline is most likely libjpeg-turbo going by the current build docs, but the README run's library is unrecorded. Recent iDCT correctness fixes (2026-09-29) should be noted; no evidence ties them to the 8950HK numbers.
